jd:
Operations analyst
Junior to mid
Regional crop-insurance and ag-weather operations desk. Analysts pull GHCN daily station extracts to sanity-check field reports and brief claims reviewers. Hiring to screen that candidates can actually use a spreadsheet on messy observational data — not just list Excel on a CV.

Day to day:
- Open station extracts and summarize temperature and precipitation for a reviewer
- Exclude missing observation codes before computing averages
- Leave labeled summary blocks colleagues can reopen and reuse
- Spot-check field reports against station minima and maxima
- Keep working files auditable instead of one-off calculator notes

Required skills:
- Can open a CSV in LibreOffice Calc or Excel
- Can compute MIN, MAX, and AVERAGE, including AVERAGEIF (or filter) when missing codes exist
- Can select a full column or data range without clicking every cell
- Can leave a labeled, formula-driven summary a reviewer can follow

Nice to have:
- Keyboard shortcuts for range selection (Ctrl+Shift+Arrow or equivalent)
- Fill or copy formulas across a summary block
- AutoFilter or AVERAGEIF for missing sentinels
- Named ranges or a dedicated summary sheet

Constraints:
- Assessment is a spreadsheet screen — not coding, GIS, modeling, or a meteorology exam
- Candidates work in stored units (tenths of °C / tenths of mm); do not require conversion
- Starter CSV and data_notes on the desktop are shared scenery, not a solved workbook
- Python or a calculator may corroborate numbers but do not replace the spreadsheet work sample
prompt: You are an operations analyst on a regional ag-weather desk. A GHCN daily extract for Petersburg 2 N, North Dakota (GHCND:USC00327027) covering calendar year 2010 is on your desktop as station_daily.csv, with a short data_notes.md. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet and produce a labeled min / max / average summary a colleague could reuse.
